subject: LatticeMed — Request: Rate-matrix exemption for bulk onramp (VP/CFO endorsement)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: LatticeMed — Request: Rate-matrix exemption for bulk onramp (VP/CFO endorsement)

Team —

Quick summary: LatticeMed (prospect moving to pilot) asked for a one-time exemption to our published rate matrix to secure a three-month bulk onramp that front-loads usage (expected 65% of Q1 usage in first 6 weeks). They are asking for a blended effective rate that sits below our standard tier floor for this volume profile.

Why this matters: win would be a strategic pilot with a large regional health system channel and potential expansion to enterprise next year. Risk is precedent-setting on starter rates and short-term revenue dilution if we don't condition the exemption properly.

What I need: VP/CFO endorsement to approve the attached rate-matrix exemption with the following guardrails (proposal attached):
- 90-day promotional tier applied to first 90 days only
- Minimum committed spend of $110k for the 90-day window; any usage beyond that converts to standard tiers
- Automatic sunset and revert to published rates after promotion window
- Countersigned PO/DocuSign required within 7 days of approval

Attachments: latticemed_proposal_v4.pdf, redwood_rate_matrix.xlsx

Please see Jonas and Ben's notes below; Marissa, flagging for your review and signoff path. I can pull together a short memo for exec signature if you want a one-pager.

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-03T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: LatticeMed — Request: Rate-matrix exemption for bulk onramp (VP/CFO endorsement)

Naomi — thanks for the write-up. A few quick thoughts:
- I like the 90-day promo + minimum-commit guardrail. To limit precedent risk, let's add a clause that the promotional rate applies only to tokens generated for the pilot product SKU X and not to other product SKUs.
- Propose a revenue protection clause: if LatticeMed fails to hit 70% of the committed spend within the first 60 days, we reserve the right to claw back the promotional differential for the remainder of the promo window.
- Legal should sign off on the PO language around data residency and audit logs; Ben can coordinate.

Ben — can you confirm legal and billing are comfortable with the proposed PO terms and the downstream accounting for promotional revenue? If not comfortable, we'll need to tighten the commitment or require a larger upfront deposit.

If Marissa wants a consolidated one-page memo for VP/CFO sign-off, I can draft in <24 hours.

- Jonas
Sr. Sales Strategy

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@latticemed.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@latticemed.com
Date: 2027-12-06T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: LatticeMed pilot commercial proposal (follow-up)

Naomi — appreciate the conversation yesterday. LatticeMed is excited to move forward but we need favorable economics to get internal procurement and the board comfortable. We would propose the following: a 90-day introductory blended rate equal to 40% below published tier floor, capped at a $150k cap (we cover overages at published tiers). In return we will commit to a six-month post-pilot pilot evaluation and an exclusive vendor recommendation to our three partner hospitals if KPIs are met.

Key asks from our procurement team:
- Net-30 payment terms on the pilot (we can provide an org-level PO)
- A termination clause allowing us to exit with 30 days notice after the 90-day promo window if KPIs are missed
- Minimal data transfer assurances (SOC2 evidence is fine)

I've attached our internal procurement tracker (we won't send the board materials yet) but want to see if Redwood can approve the 40% introductory differential with a $150k cap. If yes, we'll prepare the PO and get DocuSign moving.

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Head of Strategic Integrations
LatticeMed

Attachment: latticemed_internal_tracker.xlsx

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-10T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: LatticeMed pilot commercial proposal — endorsement request (final)

Marissa — per our earlier thread and Jonas' notes, I've updated the proposal to incorporate revenue protection and SKU scoping. The external counter is 40% below floor with a $150k cap and Net-30; procurement asked for a termination clause post-promo.

I recommend we approve an exemption limited as follows:
- 90-day promo applied to SKU "Pilot-Core" only; promo rate = 37.5% below published floor (compromise between our ask and their 40%)
- Maximum promotional liability capped at $120k (Redwood exposure) with a $30k non-refundable deposit due at signing
- Clawback provision: if 70% of committed spend not reached by day 60, promotional differential is recouped for remaining promo days
- Net-30 allowed only if procurement sends a PO and provides org-level guarantee; otherwise Net-7 invoice terms apply
- Clause: promo does not apply to any add-on services or third-party infra costs

Attachments: revised_rate_matrix_for_exec.xlsx (attached), short one-pager memo included below. Once you sign, I will route DocuSign for the PO and push legal to finalize the addendum language.
